generation_review.prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D074. LEFT separate component is one vertical stem bearing THREE horizontal bars. Bottom modestly longest; top about85–95% of bottom, middle shortest, never huge overlong base. CENTER component: one continuous vertical central stem with a small CROSS at top (vertical extends a little above its short horizontal). Just BELOW that cross is a rounded upright rectangular enclosure bisected both horizontally AND vertically, giving exactly FOUR small counters (2x2). Center vertical continues below enclosure, crosses a SHORT HORIZONTAL bar and then joins a LOWER small rounded rectangular/oval loop with exactly ONE counter. Keep both top cross and lower crossbar visible; lower crossbar roughly same width or a little wider than top crossbar. Lower loop width slightly narrower than four-counter enclosure. RIGHT UPPER separate component is a sinuous reverse-S/zigzag: a short rising hooked/slant stroke at upper left joins the top of an outward rightward bend, which turns back left then curves down and right once more; keep the attested open hooks and bends, no invented closed counter. RIGHT LOWER separate component: a large outer bowed stroke starts with a short horizontal at upper left, turns to RIGHT and DOWN and returns diagonally DOWN-LEFT. A smaller inward hook inside it bends right/down and continues into a LONG DOWNWARD stem. The returning outer diagonal CROSSES this downstem and extends to a visible free tip at LEFT of crossing. Preserve that free terminal and long right descending tail. Central lower loop must stay separate from right return. Compare all four and use coherent THX-type courses.

visual_review.method: white inspection composite compared against all available reference specimens
reading_criteria: Left three bars with bottom modestly longest, middle shortest.
Central top cross, four-counter 2x2 enclosure, lower crossbar and one lower loop counter all joined by center stem.
Right upper sinuous hooked zigzag is separate from lower bowed/crossed hook/downstem.
Lower returning diagonal continues to a free tip left of crossing; lower central loop detached from right course.
notes: All four witnesses and enlarged forms compared; native retains the coherent THX-type central inventory and both separate right parts.
Five closed center fields remain open (four upper and one lower); both crossbars and long right descender visible.
caveats: Upper and lower central crossbar lengths vary across specimens; native keeps them comparable rather than exaggerating either.

visual_reference_review.reviewer: independent visual structural review by stroke_font_engine
notes: All four witnesses compared. Left three-bar/one-vertical construction remains separate; center vertical joins uppercross and lowerbar, upper four-counter box and lower one-counter loop.
Upper right hooked zigzag is detached from lower right bowed crossing course. The lower course crosses its downstem and continues to a free lower-left tip; every short hook and loop is retained.
Left bottom bar stays modestly longer than upper levels; center four fields and lower loop stay open and right courses remain visibly separated.
limitations: Visual comparison against the supplied chart raster; not specialist paleographic certification.
Does not verify historical writing order, exact metrics, or final font stroke width.
Verdict applies only to the source PNG hash recorded here.
